_template_doc: CANONICAL WRAPPER-GENEALOGY SPECIMEN — empty template, one merge event rendered as a rooted genealogy graph that STOPS AT THE PRESENT. Spec: SCHEMA.md (same dir). Tier-3 exploratory data-harvest for Cowork+Pav ratification — NOT canon, NOT a promotion, convergence list stays 9. FILL DISCIPLINE: every node/edge carries confidence in [0,1] (SOFT, never hard categorical) + a zoom/LOD depth; certain core near the surface (the merge event + its parents) fades into a probabilistic frontier in the deep roots (down to people/place) and at the wide edges (cousins, influences) — and that frontier is FIRST-CLASS (where conjectures are cultivated; a conjecture = a low-confidence weld not yet confirmed). frame is the observer global kernels {time,space,knowledge,meaning}; emergence is frame-relative. SEARCH THE WEB, do not work from memory; cite real sources in sources[]; mark uncertain claims low-confidence. MARK DISCREPANCIES (priority disputes, contested genealogies, date/attribution conflicts, contested dormancy, and especially framework-vs-record tensions) — they are SIGNAL. bits_note is QUALITATIVE ONLY (MDL-in-bits needs latent embeddings, a LATER step — do NOT fabricate bit values). Each array below holds ONE empty exemplar element showing the shape; duplicate or delete elements as needed. EXTENDS ../latent_olympics_data/wrapper_classes_phase1.json — same organism, deeper zoom (see SCHEMA.md §4).
_status: Tier-3 WORKING specimen — exploratory data-harvest, surfaced for Cowork+Pav ratification. NOT canon, NOT a tier promotion, does NOT grow the convergence list (stays 9). All confidences are SOFT scores in [0,1]; bits are qualitative only.

extends._comment: Linkage back to the Phase-1 wrapper CLASS this merge-event specimen instantiates (SCHEMA.md §4). Same graph, deeper zoom.

child._comment: W_C — the emergent wrapper born in this merge. The trunk node. Corresponds to one Phase-1 wrapper_classes[] row, zoomed in.
child._status_enum: one of: risen | active | dormant | resurrected | stale (observer-relative lifecycle position)

utility._comment: Pav's three utility legs as prose + an enumerated affordance list.

weld._comment: The merge itself: parents -> child. The heart of the specimen and the locus of the parents-produce-W_C test. This is the frame-indexed, per-node-confidence render of ONE entry in the Phase-1 row's overlaps[].
weld._shared_sub_object_S_comment: The seam the parents fused along — what overlapped (the S of the pushout; the nesting space / Venn-lens).
weld._surprise_comment: PROSE: what W_C does that NEITHER parent predicts alone (the synergy). Prose, not a number.
weld._bits_note_comment: QUALITATIVE ONLY. A note on description-length / synergy-in-bits (e.g. 'joint description clearly shorter than either parent alone; order-of-magnitude only'). Do NOT fabricate numeric bit values — MDL-in-bits needs latent embeddings, a LATER step.
weld._survived_comment: Parent features that persisted into W_C (the stubs / procedural roots that live on).
weld._dropped_comment: Parent features lost / not carried through the weld.
weld._frame_of_weld_comment: Frame(s) in which the weld actually holds (may differ from child.frame; e.g. a weld that only holds through time). Subset of {time,space,knowledge,meaning}.
weld._lod_scale_comment: At what zoom/resolution the weld holds (e.g. 'holds at field-level grain; dissolves into many sub-welds when zoomed in').

revival._comment: If resurrected: when, by whom, and what triggered the wake. Leave blank if never dormant.

roots._comment: DOWN, in the PHYSICAL frame. The recursive descent from W_C toward people and place. Confidence FADES and depth RISES as you go deeper — this is where the certain-core -> probabilistic-frontier gradient lives.

sub_wrappers._comment: A smaller wrapper W_C is built from, recursively down. depth = levels below W_C (0 = immediate constituent; larger = deeper root, typically lower confidence).

people_0._comment: The ground kernel '(0)': a people-wrapper the deepest roots plug into, standing in the PHYSICAL frame (their time, place, environment, culture).
people_0._relation_comment: how they relate to the lineage, e.g. originator | transmitter | patron | rival | popularizer

harvest._comment: UP, in the LATENT + CULTURAL frame. What sat on top of W_C and what it spilled into. The tree grows to the present here.

descendants._comment: An emergent child: a new theory W_C (crossed with others) went on to seed.

cultural_harvest._comment: Spill into culture: the emergent clusters of this theory crossed with others.
cultural_harvest._domain_enum: one of: art | scifi | tech | other

relatives._comment: WIDE edges (SCHEMA.md §5 flag 2 — added because the brief's prose stresses 'wide relatives spanning the physical AND the latent' but the explicit field list only enumerated DOWN/UP). Cousins, influences, siblings, rivals. OPTIONAL group, flagged for ratification.

edges._relation_enum: one of: cousin | influence | sibling | rival

fuzzy_layer._comment: The LOD / confidence partition made explicit. certain_core = the trunk (high-confidence nodes/welds); frontier = the speculative/conjectural roots+branches (low-confidence — the cultivation zone). A conjecture = a weld drawn in the frontier but not yet confirmed. Complements the per-node confidence numbers above (numbers per node PLUS this curated trunk/frontier list).

discrepancies._comment: An interesting conflict in the historical record. SIGNAL, not noise (Pav's explicit ask). framework-vs-record-tension is the highest-value type — it flags where the clean two-parent weld does NOT match the messy multi-parent reality (which variables the schema is missing). Also record EXTRA real-world parents here (SCHEMA.md §5 flag 6).
discrepancies._type_enum: one of: priority-dispute | contested-genealogy | date/attribution-conflict | framework-vs-record-tension | dormancy-contested | whig-vs-revisionist

sources._comment: Citation backbone. Consult the WEB (Wikidata, OpenAlex, SEP/IEP, Wikipedia 'history of...', Mathematics Genealogy Project, nLab, Semantic Scholar, named scholarly histories). Every load-bearing field should trace here. Be honest about reliability.
sources._type_enum: one of: aggregator | encyclopedia | scholarly-history | primary
sources._reliability_comment: number [0,1] or a labelled band (e.g. 'high — peer-reviewed scholarly history')
